_schema: One entry per CDC WONDER database under dataset_versions. Keys read directly by the govex
cdc_wonder package's wonder_query(): base_url, year_selector, state_selector, groupby_options.
Keys read by cdc_wonder_puller.py: dataset_code, year_range, age_groupings, cause_axes.
groupby_options is keyed by a fixed vocabulary of ROLE names -- State, County, Year, Sex, Race,
Hispanic Origin -- so cdc_wonder_puller.build_queries() can stay database-agnostic. 'Age' is
deliberately absent: the puller injects it at run time from age_groupings, once per grouping
(as 'Age[ten_year]', 'Age[five_year]', ...) plus a plain 'Age' alias for the selected default,
so a single run can mix age resolutions (the drowning pull needs Ten-Year for county_age and
Five-Year for county_pop5yr -- see ingest.R's FIVE_TO_TEN_YEAR_AGE for why).
Every code here (D158.V5 etc.) is a WONDER-internal variable id found by loading each live
request form and reading the <label> text next to each radio/select -- CDC documents none of
them, and they are not guessable from the number (on D158, V51 is Five-Year and V52 is
Single-Year, so the suffix is not 'years of resolution'). The full raw dump of D158's form is
in wonder_form_fields.txt. The same Vxx numbering is shared by D76/D77/D157/D158 (the mortality
databases) but NOT by the natality databases, which number their variables differently.
cause_axes names the ICD-code finder variable(s) the puller may apply a cause-of-death filter
through. Each finder's widget ids all derive from that one variable: radio RO_ucd<var> or
RO_mcd<var>, list codes-<var>, buttons finder-action-<var>-Open Fully / -Open, and the
current-filter textarea <var>-fhi. Natality has no cause finder, so its cause_axes is empty
and the puller refuses a --codes argument for it.

ucd_icd10_expanded_2018_2024.description: Underlying Cause of Death, 2018-2024, Single Race (ICD-10 expanded)
_notes: This is the database the whole drowning pipeline (raw/, ingest.R) is built on.
Race V42 is Single Race 6 -- the only race variable WONDER publishes rate denominators for
(V43 = Single Race 15 and V44 = Single/Multi Race 31 give counts only).
County x Ten-Year Age Groups returns Deaths only, no Population or Crude Rate, for every
state and year (CDC-side: 'Rates and populations are not available for single-year age
groups or 10-year age groups at the county level'). Five-Year county age still reports
population, which is what ingest.R derives county population from.
Connecticut 2022+: WONDER returns only the 8 legacy CT counties (09001-09015) with
Population 'Not Available'; it has no rows for the 9 planning regions that replaced them.
CDC-side, not fixable from the scraper -- see scraper/README.md.
Same Vxx numbering as D158 except race: D76 has only the 4-category bridged Race variable
V8 (no V42/V43/V44), so its race breakdown is NOT comparable to D158's single-race one.
Overlaps D158 for 2018-2020; the two databases use different population bases for those
years, so rates differ slightly.
Smoke-tested 2026-08-25 (state_age 2019, drowning): works end to end, same footer
wording as D158. One difference for anyone writing an ingest for it: this older vintage
still flags crude rates on fewer than 20 deaths as 'Unreliable' in the rate column
(Deaths stays numeric), a marker that never occurs in the D158 files and that ingest.R's
SUPPRESSED_MARKER / MISSING_DENOM_MARKERS lists do not include.

mcd_icd10_expanded_2018_2024.description: Multiple Cause of Death, 2018-2024, Single Race (ICD-10 expanded)
_notes: Superset of D158's form with a second cause axis. 'underlying' (D157.V2, radio
RO_ucdD157.V2) filters on the underlying cause exactly like D158; 'multiple' (D157.V13,
radio RO_mcdD157.V13, 'MCD - ICD-10 Codes') counts a death if the code appears ANYWHERE on
the certificate, underlying or contributing. One axis per pull; pass --cause-axis multiple
for the latter. Both finders exist in the DOM at once and only the radio-selected one is
submitted, which is why the puller clicks the radio before touching the finder.
The MCD finder runs in WONDER's 'advanced' mode (hidden O_V13_fmode=fadv): it has two
'Selected Items' boxes (TD157.V13-AND1 / -AND2, for 'code A AND code B' queries) and NO
D157.V13-fhi mirror textarea, unlike the UCD finder. The puller therefore verifies the
applied filter from the highlighted options of codes-D157.V13 itself, which is what the
form submits (F_D157.V13); the first smoke test failed looking for the -fhi element.
D76's bridged-race layout plus D157's second cause axis; see both entries' notes.
Codes verified against the live form on 2026-08-25; not yet exercised from this repo.
Births, not deaths: no cause-of-death finder, so --codes must be omitted (the puller
raises if given one). The export carries a single Births column -- Birth Rate /
Fertility Rate are separate checkboxes on this form that the govex package does not
tick -- so there is no population/rate to derive from these files.
Role meanings shift here: 'Age' is the MOTHER's age (V1 = 9 groups, V38 = 10, V39 = 13),
'Race' and 'Hispanic Origin' are the mother's (Single Race 6 / Hispanic Origin), 'Sex' is
the INFANT's sex (D149.V3). The variable numbering is unrelated to the mortality databases.
Year is a plain <select> (SD149.V20) rather than a finder, so year_selector has no
'codes-' prefix.
Smoke-tested 2026-08-25 (state_gender 2023 and county_gender Delaware 2023): the year
select is 'multiple' so the govex deselect_all() call is fine, the Year group-by value is
'D149.V20', the export section has all three CO_show_* boxes, and the footer words things
differently from the mortality databases ('Year: 2023', 'Group By: State of Residence;
Sex of Infant'; the state filter line is 'States: Delaware (10)' as on mortality) -- hence
the footer block above, which the puller's export validation reads.
Same layout and caveats as natality_expanded_2016_2024, with a longer year range and
fewer medical variables. Race defaults to Mother's Single Race 6 (D66.V42); the bridged
Mother's Race (D66.V2) is also offered and can be swapped in with groupby_overrides.
Codes and the footer block are carried over from the expanded entry (same form family);
this entry itself has not been run from here yet -- smoke-test before any full pull.
